lessons.text: For both MU and the SOX, build the gap range so the latest pre-market print sits inside it, with room beyond that print in the direction pre-market has been moving, instead of letting the range end at or short of that print.

evidence.count: 4 of 7 gap calls (3 of 5 MU, 1 of 2 SOX) opened past the far edge of the called range in the direction of the move; on 2 of those days the brief's own last pre-

lessons.text: List at most two MU levels on each side, the ones nearest the called open, and drop deeper items such as the 200-day average, round-number bear-case references and third or fourth resistances unless they sit within a few percent of the called open.

evidence.count: 15 of 18 MU levels listed third or deeper on a side were untested; 24 of 38 MU levels overall were untested

lessons.text: During a run of down days, present every MU support as a level to watch rather than a floor, and drop labels like 'line in the sand' or 'support the price is sitting on', because no listed support has held in this window.

evidence.count: 0 of 15 MU supports held (10 broke, 5 untested); every support broke on 2 of 5 days, and the named 'line in the sand' and 200-day support both broke

lessons.text: For the SOX, include at least one level on each side close to the called open, and re-label any level the called gap would jump past (for example a support sitting above a called gap-down open) instead of listing it on its old side.

evidence.count: 11 of 11 SOX levels untested; on 2026-11-05 both listed supports sat above the called opening range
